challenges.name: maps-structs-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: nil maps and structs inside maps
challenges.description: Decide where a nil map stops working, then pick the ways to count parcels in a map that compile and do not panic.

questions.question:
Stats is struct{ Delivered int }. What happens when this runs?

var byDistrict map[string]Stats
fmt.Println(len(byDistrict), byDistrict["q1"].Delivered)
byDistrict["q1"] = Stats{Delivered: 1}
fmt.Println("saved")
questions.explanation: byDistrict is declared but never made, so it is a nil map. Reading a nil map is allowed: len is 0 and a missing key gives the zero Stats, so the first line prints 0 0. Writing to a nil map is not: the assignment panics with "assignment to entry in nil map", and "saved" is never printed. It compiles fine - the compiler does not track whether a map was made. Create the map with make(map[string]Stats) or a literal map[string]Stats{} before the first write.

options.text: It prints 0 0, then panics: assignment to entry in nil map
It panics on the first Println, because the map is nil
It does not compile: the map must be made before it is used

questions.question: Stats is struct{ Delivered int } and Key is struct{ District, Status string }. Which snippets compile, run without a panic and leave a count of 1 for q1? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: counts["q1"]++ reads the zero value 0 for the missing key, adds 1 and stores it: the standard counting idiom. map[string]*Stats{"q1": {}} stores a pointer to a new Stats (inside a map literal, &Stats{} may be written as {}), so p["q1"].Delivered++ changes the struct the pointer points to. A struct key such as Key{"q1", "delivered"} works because structs whose fields are comparable can be compared with ==, so they can be map keys - often simpler than a map of maps. stats["q1"].Delivered++ on a map[string]Stats does not compile (the compiler says: cannot assign to struct field stats["q1"].Delivered in map): m[k] gives a copy that cannot be assigned. And q["q1"].Delivered++ on an empty map[string]*Stats reads a nil pointer for the missing key and panics with "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference".

challenges.name: district-delivery-report
challenges.title: Build the daily district report from tracking events
challenges.description: The tracking service records an event every time a parcel changes status, so one parcel has several events during the day (out for delivery, failed, out again, delivered ...). Write report and busiest for the evening district report: keep only the last event of every parcel, count the parcels per district by their last status, return the districts sorted by name, and find the district with the most parcels (the first by name on a tie). Map iteration order is random, so the order must come from your code. The test runner reads the events and prints one line per district and the busiest district.

tests.name: The example: the last event of each parcel counts
tests.input:
SP-3001 q1 out
SP-3002 q3 out
SP-3001 q1 delivered
SP-3002 q3 failed
SP-3002 q3 returned
tests.expected:
q1: parcels 1, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 0
q3: parcels 1, delivered 0, failed 0, returned 1
busiest: q1, parcels 1

tests.name: Districts sorted by name; a parcel still out counts only as a parcel
tests.input:
SP-3101 thu-duc out
SP-3102 binh-thanh out
SP-3103 q1 out
SP-3104 q1 out
SP-3101 thu-duc delivered
SP-3103 q1 delivered
SP-3105 go-vap delivered
SP-3104 q1 failed
tests.expected:
binh-thanh: parcels 1, delivered 0, failed 0, returned 0
go-vap: parcels 1, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 0
q1: parcels 2, delivered 1, failed 1, returned 0
thu-duc: parcels 1, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 0
busiest: q1, parcels 2

tests.name: A tie for busiest goes to the first district by name
tests.input:
SP-3201 q3 delivered
SP-3202 q3 delivered
SP-3203 go-vap failed
SP-3204 go-vap delivered
SP-3205 q1 returned
tests.expected:
go-vap: parcels 2, delivered 1, failed 1, returned 0
q1: parcels 1, delivered 0, failed 0, returned 1
q3: parcels 2, delivered 2, failed 0, returned 0
busiest: go-vap, parcels 2

tests.name: A parcel that failed, went out again and was delivered
tests.input:
SP-3301 binh-thanh out
SP-3301 binh-thanh failed
SP-3301 binh-thanh out
SP-3301 binh-thanh delivered
SP-3302 binh-thanh out
SP-3302 binh-thanh failed
SP-3303 q1 out
tests.expected:
binh-thanh: parcels 2, delivered 1, failed 1, returned 0
q1: parcels 1, delivered 0, failed 0, returned 0
busiest: binh-thanh, parcels 2

tests.name: Interleaved events across three districts
tests.input:
SP-3401 q3 out
SP-3402 thu-duc out
SP-3403 thu-duc out
SP-3404 q3 out
SP-3402 thu-duc delivered
SP-3401 q3 failed
SP-3403 thu-duc failed
SP-3405 thu-duc out
SP-3401 q3 returned
SP-3404 q3 delivered
SP-3403 thu-duc returned
SP-3406 q1 delivered
tests.expected:
q1: parcels 1, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 0
q3: parcels 2, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 1
thu-duc: parcels 3, delivered 1, failed 0, returned 1
busiest: thu-duc, parcels 3
